NDIA-ICT-AAP-001
1. Governance and accountability
Governance, roles and accountability

NDIA must operate ICT A&A under approved governance that supports NDIA's statutory functions, assigns accountable roles and delegations to the Accountable Authority, CISO, Authorising Officers and system owners, and escalates material ICT security risks through approved audit, risk, Board and ministerial reporting channels where required.
Applies to all ICT systems and all A&A decisions.

2. A&A lifecycle and authorisation gates
ISM-aligned A&A lifecycle and authorisation decision

No NDIA ICT system may process, store or communicate government information in production until the Authorising Officer has used an ISM-aligned A&A lifecycle, considered residual security risk and granted an Authority to Operate; all authorisation decisions must be recorded in the authorised systems register.
Applies before production use, reauthorisation or material change.

3. Risk management and residual risk acceptance
Risk appetite, ownership and internal control

Each system must have an SRMP and named risk owner or steward that assesses residual, shared and legacy-technology risks against NDIA's risk appetite, tolerance and internal control requirements, with approved treatments or compensating controls for risks outside tolerance.
Applies to system, shared, supplier, legacy and residual risks.

System definition, boundary, classification and criticality

Applies during project initiation, security categorisation, assessment scoping and reauthorisation.

5. Control baseline and implementation
Baseline security controls and access safeguards

Systems must implement the approved control baseline before authorisation, including ISM controls, Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, protective DNS or equivalent controls, approved cryptography, access control, unique identity, MFA, restricted administration and tested backups; any gap requires approved compensating controls, remediation and residual risk acceptance.
Applies to controls selected for all systems, tailored by classification, sensitivity and risk.

6. Information handling, privacy and lawful disclosure
Privacy, protected information and lawful use or disclosure

Systems handling personal information or protected Agency information must apply privacy by design, reasonable security safeguards, role-based access, logging, monitoring and data-loss controls, and allow collection, use, disclosure, sharing, outsourcing, retention and destruction only for authorised purposes.
Applies to systems handling personal information, protected Agency information or information obtained by officials.

7. Assessment evidence and audit trail
Control assessment evidence and auditability

A&A decisions must be supported by reliable, current and auditable evidence, including control assessment results, SARs, IRAP and Essential Eight evidence where applicable, configuration or test artefacts, risk records and complete approval trails; unsupported assertions are not sufficient.
Applies to all assessment claims, ATO evidence packs and audit trails.

Security testing, vulnerability management and remediation

Systems must complete risk-based security testing before production and after significant change, operate vulnerability disclosure and triage processes, and track findings, deficiencies and IRAP recommendations in a POA&M until closed, treated or explicitly risk accepted.
Applies before production, after significant change and during the ATO period.

14. Records, retention and disposal
Records, metadata, retention and secure disposal

Systems must identify and preserve required records, datasets, logs, metadata, security labels and access-rights information, and must retain, transfer, alter, de-identify, sanitise or dispose of information and assets only through authorised records, privacy, Archives Act and ISM processes.
Applies to system records, A&A records, datasets, logs, metadata, assets and decommissioning activities.

15. Conditional CDR obligations
Conditional Consumer Data Right obligations

If CDR obligations apply, the system must define the CDR data environment, implement mandatory CDR security controls, assess NDIA and outsourced controls, retain required logs, complete internal and conformance testing before activation, report deficiencies and incidents, and maintain ongoing CDR conformance.
Applies only where the system handles CDR data or participates in CDR.

16. Conditional SOCI, SOGS and critical infrastructure obligations
Conditional SOCI, SOGS and critical infrastructure obligations

If SOCI, SOGS or critical infrastructure obligations apply, the ATO package and SRMP must confirm applicability, critical asset status, data service provider notifications, protected-information handling, risk management program alignment, register or ownership reporting, enhanced cyber obligations, mandatory cyber reporting and government assistance escalation.
Applies only where SOCI, Systems of Government Significance or critical infrastructure obligations apply.
